title: Welcome to Unit 7: How Proteins Become Living Machines!
customHtml:
Inside every one of your cells, thousands of proteins are folding from linear chains of amino acids into precise three-dimensional shapes — and they're doing it in milliseconds, without instructions. The shape determines everything: whether a protein becomes a muscle fiber, an oxygen carrier, an enzyme that breaks down sugar, or an antibody that fights infection. Get the shape wrong, and the protein doesn't just fail — it can cause disease.

This unit explores one of biology's deepest puzzles: how does a one-dimensional string of amino acids "know" which three-dimensional shape to take? You'll meet the principles behind protein folding, learn why some proteins misfold, and see how scientists have started predicting and designing protein structures from sequence alone.

The science you're about to study has applications in:

  • Designing new medicines — almost every modern drug works by binding to a precisely-shaped pocket on a protein
  • Understanding diseases of misfolding — Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS, and prion diseases all involve proteins that take the wrong shape
  • Vaccine development — mRNA vaccines work by instructing your cells to produce a precisely-folded viral protein for your immune system to recognise
  • Enzyme engineering for industry — laundry detergents, biofuels, even removing CO₂ from the atmosphere
  • AI and structural biology — AlphaFold's breakthrough showed that machine learning can predict protein structures from sequence with near-experimental accuracy

You'll see that proteins are not just static cartoons in a textbook, but the dynamic, shape-shifting machines that make life work.
